newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Vodaphone wants Digicall to continue.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Vodaphone wants Digicall to continue.

text.p: Mobile telecommunications firm Vodaphone Group said on Monday it hoped to achieve a financial restructuring of its largest Australian reseller, Digicall Group Ltd, and keep the company operating.
The U.K.-based company said it had appointed Arthur Andersen partner Martin Madden as receiver and manager of the listed company to begin the restructuring.
Madden told Reuters that Vodaphone was owed about A$50 million and that he was in the early stage of investigating Digicall's financial position.
Digicall shares were suspended last Friday.

Madden said it appeared that while Digicall had about 100,000 subscribers, the company would continue dealings with 75,000 to 80,000 only as the remainder were suspect due to various problems such as bad debts and fraud.
"I am still trying to get access to up to date financial information," he said of Digicall. But the company did not make a profit in the 1995/96 financial year, he said.

Vodaphone managing director John Rohan said the company had a business-as-usual policy towards Digicall customers. "It is our desire that Digicall continue as a service provider and play a major role in the fast-growing mobile digital market."
